name: Sanctuary of Aphrodite
note: Aphrodite goes to her precinct and altar at Paphos, Odyssey 8.362–363

name: Heraion of Samos
note: Herodotus 3.60 calls its later temple the largest he knew

name: Sanctuary of Apollo
note: the standing temple is of the 4th century BCE

name: Temple of Poseidon
note: one of the earliest monumental temples in Greece; seat of the Isthmian Games

name: Temple of Hera
note: the Hermes of Praxiteles was found in it in 1877

name: Terrace of the Lions
note: a Naxian dedication in the sanctuary of Apollo's birthplace

name: Temple of Artemis
note: Croesus gave most of its columns, Herodotus 1.92; burned in 356 BCE; its rebuilt successor was counted among the Seven Wonders

name: Oracle of Zeus
note: Achilles prays to Zeus of Dodona, Iliad 16.233–235

name: Temple of Zeus
note: held the gold-and-ivory Zeus of Pheidias, c. 435 BCE

name: Metopes of the Temple of Zeus
note: the twelve labours, six over each porch

name: Temple of Apollo Epikourios
note: Pausanias 8.41.9 names Iktinos as its architect

name: Temple of Hephaestus
note: the best-preserved Doric temple in Greece

name: Parthenon
note: its west pediment showed the contest with Poseidon, Pausanias 1.24.5

name: Temple of Poseidon
note: on the cape at the southern tip of Attica

name: Temple of Ares
note: moved to the Agora and rebuilt there in the late 1st century BCE

name: Telesterion
note: on the site of the temple the Hymn to Demeter has her command, lines 270–274, and of the rites she teaches, 473–479

name: Theatre of Dionysus Eleuthereus
note: the Bacchae was first staged here in 405 BCE, in the theatre as it was before the stone rebuilding
